specification_compliance: I6 (the r6 F2 sequence A fail → B success → A): YouTubeEmbed.tsx:128-130 runs before the load effect at :265, because effects run in declaration order. When videoId changes it clears failedVideoIdRef, unless the ref already holds the new id. On the return to A the ref is null, so the guard at :267 lets the load run and setLoadFailed(false) happens. A then either plays or fails again and shows the link card (:381-384, :454-455). No empty box remains for this sequence.

§3 191 (a link card is not turned back into a player by a youtubeUi toggle or a new callback identity): the clearing effect depends only on [videoId]. On a rerun of the load effect for the same id, the ref still equals videoId and the effect returns at :267 while loadFailed stays true (it is set together with the ref at :383-384), so the link card stays. A fileId change with the same URL also keeps the link card.
I7: the restricted and playing paths are unchanged by this round. setEmbedRestricted(false) is still reset only past the guard.
The other invariants (I1-I5, I8-I10) are untouched by this fix commit. This round changes only YouTubeEmbed.tsx and EmbedLinkCard.test.tsx inside the media_import submodule.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: Two different .loft files that point to the same YouTube video id share the no-retry guard when one embed instance moves between them. After the first file's API load failed, the second file shows the link card without a new load attempt.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It needs two .loft files for the same video played one after the other in the same embed instance, right after a transient script failure. The user sees the link card, not a blank box.

regression_risks: When loadFailed is true and the URL changes while window.YT is already present (for example loaded by another embed instance), loadYouTubeIframeApi resolves at once (loadYouTubeIframeApi.ts:38-39). The load effect's .then may then run before the re-render that mounts hostRef. It would return at YouTubeEmbed.tsx:277 and leave an empty box. The same ordering exists for the embedRestricted → new URL path and predates this round. I did not confirm React's flush order in a real browser, and the tests wrap rerenders in act(), which hides it.
The clearing effect relies on being declared before the load effect. Moving it below line 265 would make the A→B→A return-to-A case fail again. The new test would catch that.
test_coverage: EmbedLinkCard.test.tsx adds 'returning to a URL whose load failed earlier tries the load again' (A fail → B success → A). It asserts that a second YT.Player is constructed. Removing the clearing effect at YouTubeEmbed.tsx:128-130 leaves constructed at 1 and fails the test. Moving the effect below the load effect has the same result.
The new test does not assert the rendered output for A on the return (a player box, or the link card if A fails again). It also does not cover A fail → B fail → A.

The existing test 'shows the link card for a viewer whose stored skin is YouTube's' still covers no retry on a rerun for the same id. Deleting the guard at :267 would make that test fail only if the effect reran for the same id, so the guard against retrying on a youtubeUi toggle is covered only indirectly.

trajectory: One fix round (31294ed45) came after r6. It adds a new branch: an effect keyed on [videoId] that clears failedVideoIdRef. That branch patches the failedVideoIdRef guard, a state with an early return that an earlier round had added so a failed load would not retry on a youtubeUi toggle. The guard then needed a reset rule for the case r6 F2 found. So the retry policy of YouTubeEmbed is being patched with extra state rather than designed: a ref plus an ordering-dependent reset effect beside loadFailed, when a single 'failed for id X' state could carry both. The round removes no branch or state. It closes the A→B→A empty box, and I found no new invariant break.
